subject: F792910_00_SER / F792910_00_REA (v3 diagnostic)

serializable.cockroachdb_note: 0 40001 errors observed: CockroachDB SERIALIZABLE resolves write-write conflicts via read-timestamp refresh rather than aborting, when the refresh succeeds. The 181 serialization errors in latency.json came from the sustained high-frequency contention harness where refresh fails more often.

read_committed.cockroachdb_note: 0 forks despite no serialization: CockroachDB RC acquires pessimistic intent-based write locks on DML, serializing concurrent writes to the same row. This prevents the lost-update fork that PostgreSQL RC would produce.

conclusion: Both isolation levels produced trusted=1 in all 5 trials with 12 concurrent writers. CockroachDB RC does NOT fork because it uses pessimistic write locks even under RC — unlike PostgreSQL RC which would allow the classic lost-update fork. SERIALIZABLE does NOT produce 40001 in this workload because CockroachDB's read-timestamp refresh resolves conflicts without aborting; aborts occur under sustained contention (181 errors observed in latency.json harness). SERIALIZABLE remains required for PQBS for three independent reasons: (1) consistent snapshot reads for S1 cluster-mean computation — RC allows non-repeatable reads that corrupt anomaly scoring, (2) explicit 40001 errors under sustained contention that force proper retry handling, (3) correctness guarantee against future CockroachDB implementation changes and portable reasoning about isolation semantics.
